title: Email Not Sending
description: Diagnose wp_mail failures affecting contact forms, WooCommerce orders, and admin notifications.

steps.title: Identify Which Emails Fail
steps.instructions: Determine if all emails fail or only specific types (forms, WooCommerce, core notifications). Test wp_mail with a logging plugin like WP Mail Logging.

steps.title: Review Mail Logs and SMTP Errors
steps.instructions: Check SMTP plugin logs, host mail queue, and bounce messages. Look for authentication failures, relay denied, or quota exceeded errors.

steps.title: Configure Reliable SMTP Provider
steps.instructions: Set up SendGrid, Mailgun, Amazon SES, or host SMTP with TLS on port 587. Avoid port 25 on shared hosting — it is often blocked.

steps.title: Add SPF, DKIM, and DMARC Records
steps.instructions: Publish DNS records required by your mail provider. Use mail-tester.com or similar to verify deliverability score before closing the ticket.

steps.title: Fix From Name and Reply-To Headers
steps.instructions: Form plugins may override From with visitor addresses — many hosts reject this. Set a domain From address and use Reply-To for the submitter.

steps.title: Check for Plugin Hook Conflicts
steps.instructions: Multiple plugins filtering wp_mail can break headers. Disable other mail plugins temporarily and test with a simple wp_mail() call.

steps.title: Verify End-to-End Delivery
steps.instructions: Submit a contact form, place a test order, and trigger a password reset. Confirm emails arrive in inbox (not spam) within expected time.
